Inspect the structure of an expression

Source: R/ast.R
z3_inspect.Rd

Z3 expressions are trees. z3_kind() classifies a node:

Usage

z3_kind(x)

z3_decl(x)

z3_args(x)

z3_num_args(x)

z3_decl_info(decl)

z3_is_const(x)

z3_is_numeral(x)

z3_is_app(x)

z3_is_quantifier(x)

z3_quantifier_info(x)

z3_var_index(x)

z3_bound_var(ctx, index, sort)

z3_apply(decl, ...)

Arguments

x

A z3_expr.

decl

A z3_func_decl or z3_function.

ctx

A z3_context() (unused when sort is given).

index

De Bruijn index of a bound variable.

sort

Sort of the bound variable.

...

Arguments for z3_apply(): expressions, R values, or lists of them.

Value

See Details.

Details

  • "numeral": a number (Int, Real, bit-vector or floating point value);

  • "app": an application of a function declaration to arguments, including constants (no arguments) and built-in operators;

  • "var": a bound variable inside a quantifier body, identified by its de Bruijn index;

  • "quantifier": forall, exists or lambda.

z3_decl() returns the function declaration at the head of an application (numerals included), z3_args() its arguments, and z3_decl_info() describes a declaration: its name, kind (such as "add", "le", "and", "bvadd" or "uninterpreted"), domain, range and indexed parameters (for example the bounds of an extract). Kinds that only some Z3 versions define are reported as "other".

z3_quantifier_info() returns the type, bound variable names and sorts, body (with bound variables as "var" nodes), weight and patterns of a quantifier. z3_var_index() gives a bound variable's de Bruijn index; z3_bound_var() creates one, for building bodies for z3_substitute_vars() and z3_substitute_funs().

Examples

ctx <- z3_context()
x <- z3_int(ctx, "x")
e <- x + 2 * x^2
z3_kind(e)
#> [1] "app"
z3_decl_info(z3_decl(e))$kind
#> [1] "add"
z3_args(e)
#> [[1]]
#> <z3_expr Int> x
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> <z3_expr Int> (* 2 x x)
#> 
z3_kind(z3_int_val(ctx, 3))
#> [1] "numeral"
q <- z3_forall(x, x * 0 == 0)
z3_quantifier_info(q)$names
#> [1] "x"
